{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: docs/generated-sequences-architecture.md\n+# Generated Sequences Architecture\n+\n+## Opening\n+\n+Reigh already has a safe v1 path for AI-authored animation beats: the browser editor asks `supabase/functions/ai-generate-sequence/index.ts` for trusted sequence drafts, validates the model response against a narrow draft schema, and inserts the result as ordinary timeline data. That path is intentionally data-only. The model may choose from trusted `clipType` values, `hold`, and JSON params, but it may not return TSX, imports, raw URLs, arbitrary animation references, or executable render logic.\n+\n+This document plans how to add more flexible AI-generated animation sequences without weakening that baseline. The target architecture must support three levels of expressiveness over time: the existing trusted structured drafts, declarative schema-sequences that compile into normal timeline clips, and generated Remotion modules that execute only in worker render infrastructure. Those lanes are additive. The current trusted sequence creator remains the default safe editor behavior until later rollout decisions explicitly enable another lane.\n+\n+The load-bearing implementation boundary today is that persisted timelines are still `TimelineConfig` plus `AssetRegistry` data. Current UI insertion code in `src/tools/video-editor/lib/sequence-drafts.ts` converts a validated draft into rows, clip metadata, clip order, and ordinary timeline edits. Current render materialization in `src/tools/video-editor/sequences/materialize.ts` resolves asset-key params into component-facing URLs at render payload time without mutating persisted params. Any new lane must preserve that persistence invariant unless a later migration explicitly changes it.\n+\n+## Current-State Map\n+\n+### Trusted v1 sequence authoring\n+\n+- `src/tools/video-editor/components/SequenceCreator/SequenceCreatorPanel.tsx` is the browser entry point. It sends the user prompt, selected or attached clips, the allowed asset registry subset, and allowed trusted clip types to the `ai-generate-sequence` edge function.\n+- `supabase/functions/ai-generate-sequence/index.ts` authenticates the user, rate-limits the request, builds model messages, calls Anthropic, extracts `drafts`, attempts a JSON-only repair pass when extraction fails, then validates each raw draft before returning it to the editor.\n+- `supabase/functions/ai-generate-sequence/sequence-validation.ts` is the edge-side validator. It only accepts root keys `clipType`, `hold`, and `params`; rejects generated-code fields such as `code`, `component`, `jsx`, `tsx`, `imports`, `source`, and `render`; rejects animation-reference fields such as `animation`, `transition`, `entrance`, and `exit`; rejects raw URLs; and restricts asset-valued params to selected or attached registry asset keys.\n+- `src/tools/video-editor/sequences/validation.ts` mirrors the trusted draft contract in the frontend. It exists so the editor can reason about drafts using the same data-only assumptions as the edge function.\n+- `src/tools/video-editor/sequences/metadata.ts` defines the trusted sequence catalog. At the time of this map, the catalog includes `image-jump`, `section-hook`, `art-card`, `resource-card`, and `cta-card`, all under the trusted `2rp` sequence theme.\n+- `src/tools/video-editor/lib/sequence-drafts.ts` inserts or replaces sequence drafts as normal timeline clips. It sets `clipType`, `hold`, and `params`, updates row actions and clip order, resolves overlaps, and selects the inserted clip. It does not persist code artifacts.\n+\n+### Current renderer split\n+\n+- `src/tools/video-editor/lib/renderRouter.ts` owns render-button routing. `decideRenderRoute()` sends pure native clips to the existing client renderer and sends timelines containing registered theme-package clip types to `banodoco_render_timeline`.\n+- The native client-renderable set is `media`, `text`, `effect-layer`, `hold`, plus legacy clips with no `clipType`.\n+- The Banodoco route is selected when a clip `clipType` exists in `THEME_PACKAGE_REGISTRY`; mixed timelines containing both theme-package clips and media/native clips also route to Banodoco.\n+- `src/tools/video-editor/compositions/TimelineRenderer.tsx` separately renders actual timeline playback. It dispatches native clips to Reigh-native components, dispatches registered sequence/theme clip types through `SEQUENCE_COMPONENT_REGISTRY`, and uses `UnknownClipPlaceholderSequence` for unsupported clip types instead of silently rendering black output.\n+\n+### Unknown-clip routing hazard\n+\n+`decideRenderRoute()` currently treats unknown `clipType` values as media-equivalent, so the route remains `client` and the renderer relies on the loud placeholder fallback. That behavior is reasonable for mistyped or not-yet-installed theme packages, but it is unsafe as the only discriminator for generated Remotion modules. A novel generated-code clip type could accidentally stay on the client route. Generated-code routing therefore cannot be based on inventing new `clipType` strings alone; it needs explicit lane metadata and tests that prove unknown or absent clip types do not imply generated-code execution.\n+\n+### Persistence and import invariants\n+\n+- The editor and edge-agent persistence model is ordinary timeline JSON. `src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts` defines `TimelineConfig` with `output`, `clips`, optional `tracks`, optional `pinnedShotGroups`, and optional theme fields, plus `AssetRegistry` as `assets: Record<string, AssetRegistryEntry>`.\n+- `supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/db.ts` persists editor/agent updates through `saveTimelineConfigVersioned()`, which calls `update_timeline_config_versioned` with a `TimelineConfig` and expected version.\n+- `supabase/functions/timeline-import/handler.ts` validates imported timelines against `@banodoco/timeline-schema`, checks `project_id` and `timeline_id` UUIDs, verifies project ownership, checks existing row ownership, and writes through versioned RPCs.\n+- `supabase/functions/timeline-import/validate.ts` treats `asset_registry` as a Reigh-specific envelope and verifies only that `asset_registry.assets` is object-shaped. Import may include an asset registry, but it still writes into the existing `timelines.config` and `timelines.asset_registry` fields.\n+\n+## Non-Negotiable Constraints\n+\n+- The trusted v1 sequence creator remains the default path. Future schema or code lanes must be gated additions, not replacements for `SequenceCreatorPanel` and the current `ai-generate-sequence` draft flow.\n+- Trusted drafts remain data-only. The v1 validator must continue rejecting generated code, raw URLs, imports, arbitrary animation refs, unknown top-level fields, and asset references outside the selected or attached registry set.\n+- Browser editor execution must stay non-code. Generated Remotion module source must never execute in the Reigh browser editor; browser preview can use status, thumbnails, rendered previews, placeholders, or schema-derived fallback views.\n+- Persisted compiled output should continue to be ordinary `TimelineConfig` and `AssetRegistry` wherever possible. Proposed generated-sequence artifact records, buckets, manifests, and lane metadata must be additive links around the timeline, not a mandatory rewrite of existing timeline rows.\n+- Render routing for generated code must use explicit lane metadata, not only `clipType`. The current unknown-clip fallback means a new clip type alone can route to the client renderer.\n+- Existing render paths must remain operational during rollout and rollback. Disabling schema-sequences or generated modules must leave trusted v1 sequence drafts and native client rendering usable.\n+- Timeline imports and ArtAgents outputs must converge on the same timeline schema contract before broad rollout. Hand-maintained parallel schema shapes are not acceptable for generated sequence interchange.\n+- Any generated-code lane must execute in a worker sandbox with bounded dependencies, validated manifests, explicit asset access, timeouts, and structured failure output.\n+- Existing timelines require compatibility. Current rows with trusted sequence clip types must continue to load, edit, preview, import, and render without mandatory migration.\n+\n+## Settled Decisions\n+\n+- **SD-GENSEQ-001** — Preserve trusted v1 as the default sequence path. _load_bearing: true_\n+  Rationale: The existing path has a narrow validator, data-only draft output, editor insertion logic, and known render behavior. It is the safety baseline for every future lane.\n+\n+- **SD-GENSEQ-002** — Keep trusted draft output data-only. _load_bearing: true_\n+  Rationale: The current validator explicitly rejects code, raw URLs, imports, and arbitrary animation references. Relaxing that validator would collapse the safety distinction between trusted drafts and generated modules.\n+\n+- **SD-GENSEQ-003** — Route generated Remotion modules by explicit lane metadata, not novel `clipType`. _load_bearing: true_\n+  Rationale: `decideRenderRoute()` currently treats unknown clip types as client-renderable fallback so the loud placeholder can surface unsupported clips. Generated-code routing needs a discriminator that cannot be mistaken for ordinary unknown media.\n+\n+- **SD-GENSEQ-004** — Keep compiled timeline persistence on `TimelineConfig` plus `AssetRegistry` unless a later migration explicitly changes it. _load_bearing: true_\n+  Rationale: Editor commits, edge-agent saves, timeline import, render payload building, and existing rows already depend on these persistence fields.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

Whether a clip can be authored, previewed, or rendered is decided by trusted sequence validation, schema-sequence validation, render registry checks, and the explicit generated-sequence lane metadata described later.\n \n+## Generated Sequence Artifact Discriminant\n+\n+Generated sequence artifacts need an explicit discriminator in persisted clip data. The discriminator is not the clip type. The current render router treats unknown `clipType` values as client-renderable fallback so unsupported clips can surface through `UnknownClipPlaceholderSequence`; generated Remotion modules must never rely on that fallback path.\n+\n+### Clip metadata contract\n+\n+Use `clip.generation` as the additive metadata envelope for generated sequence provenance and routing. The base timeline schema should keep `clip.generation` open, but generated sequence validators and the render router must recognize these keys:\n+\n+```ts\n+type SequenceLane = 'trusted_v1' | 'schema_sequence' | 'remotion_module';\n+\n+type GeneratedSequenceGeneration = {\n+  sequence_lane?: SequenceLane;\n+  artifact_id?: string;\n+  artifact_version?: number;\n+  compiler_version?: string;\n+  source_kind?: 'trusted_draft' | 'schema_sequence' | 'remotion_module';\n+};\n+```\n+\n+Lane meanings:\n+\n+- `trusted_v1`: optional provenance for the current trusted sequence path. Existing v1 trusted draft clips do not need a migration and may omit `clip.generation` entirely.\n+- `schema_sequence`: a proposed declarative, non-code sequence artifact that compiles into normal timeline clips and params. It may link back to an artifact with `artifact_id`, but runtime rendering should still use compiled ordinary timeline data.\n+- `remotion_module`: a proposed generated Remotion module artifact. Any clip in this lane must include a non-empty `clip.generation.artifact_id`, and render routing must treat it as worker-only generated code.\n+\n+For generated Remotion modules, the load-bearing invariant is:\n+\n+```ts\n+clip.generation?.sequence_lane === 'remotion_module'\n+  && typeof clip.generation?.artifact_id === 'string'\n+  && clip.generation.artifact_id.length > 0\n+```\n+\n+A clip that lacks `clip.generation.sequence_lane` is not a generated Remotion module, even when its `clipType` is unknown. This may require a new blocked/error route or an error field on `RenderRouteDecision`; either shape is acceptable only if callers cannot proceed to the client renderer.\n+- Keep current unknown-clip fallback behavior for clips without the generated-module lane. Unknown `clipType` plus no lane should continue to route to the existing client placeholder path.\n+- Keep legacy clips with absent `clipType` and no generated-module lane client-renderable.\n+\n+The ordering matters. A generated module with a novel `clipType` should route by `clip.generation.sequence_lane`, not by registry membership, and not by the unknown-clip fallback branch.\n+\n+### Render-router test expectations\n+\n+Update `src/tools/video-editor/lib/renderRouter.test.ts` alongside the router change. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked how remotion itself acquires delay handles in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/iframe.js:8-18`. remotion's own components create the handle synchronously with `usestate(() => delayrender(...))`; the plan says 'calls delayrender() on mount', which reads like an effect-time action and leaves the initial-frame blocking behavior underspecified compared with the actual library pattern. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

A deterministic compiler plus input/output validation keeps this lane closer to normal timeline authoring.\n+\n+- **SD-GENSEQ-011** — Execute generated Remotion modules only in a worker sandbox, never in the Reigh browser editor. _load_bearing: true_\n+  Rationale: Generated modules may contain code, imports, and render logic. That risk belongs behind artifact validation, dependency policy, resource limits, and worker isolation rather than in the interactive editor.\n*** End Patch\n"

Generated sequence support should extend that payload contract instead of creating an unrelated render path.\n+\n+Route selection requirements:\n+\n+- Native and legacy timelines without generated module lanes may continue to route to the client renderer.\n+- Registered theme-package timelines may continue to route to `banodoco_render_timeline`.\n+- Valid `remotion_module` clips must route to the worker/orchestrator path by lane metadata before clip type checks.\n+- Malformed `remotion_module` clips must produce a blocked/error decision, never a client render.\n+- Schema-sequence clips should route according to their compiled clip types unless they also contain a generated module lane, because schema-sequences are already compiled into ordinary timeline data.\n+- Route decisions must include reason values that distinguish theme-package rendering, generated module rendering, malformed module metadata, and mixed timelines.\n+\n+### Worker payload and execution\n+\n+The worker render payload for generated modules should include the same base data as `BanodocoRenderTimelinePayload`, plus proposed generated-artifact references:\n+\n+- `timeline_id`, `project_id`, `correlation_id`, and user authorization context.\n+- Materialized `timeline` validated against the aligned shared schema.\n+- `assets` as the current asset registry envelope.\n+- A list of generated module artifact ids and versions required by the timeline.\n+- Render policy metadata, including dependency allowlist version, network policy, resource limits, and timeout.\n+\n+The worker must validate the payload again before execution. (flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the actual export surface in `supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/llm/messages.ts` and its consumers. step 6 says to 'remove local `isrecord`' from `messages.ts` and import it from `utils.ts`, but without also preserving `messages.ts` as an exporter or rewiring `index.ts`, `db.ts`, `tool-calls.ts`, and `selectedclips.ts`, that change would break the module graph immediately. (flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the render-gating cleanup plan against remotion's runtime exports in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/cancel-render.js:46-70`. `cancelrender()` stores an error and throws to abort the render; it is not a benign cleanup for an abandoned `delayrender` handle, so step 2's instruction to call `cancelrender(handle)` on unmount is technically wrong and would abort preview or export with an error. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked how remotion itself acquires delay handles in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/iframe.js:8-18`. remotion's own components create the handle synchronously with `usestate(() => delayrender(...))`; the plan says 'calls delayrender() on mount', which reads like an effect-time action and leaves the initial-frame blocking behavior underspecified compared with the actual library pattern. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

        Debt watch items (do not make these worse):
- [DEBT] agent-chat-rendering: removing the duplicate assistant turn may hide message_user text if the frontend only renders assistant-role turns as chat bubbles. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] agent-chat-undo-integration: agent chat edits arrive via query invalidation/realtime polling and will bypass the undo stack because those paths are marked skiphistory. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] agent-tool-utils: agent-tool-utils: step 6 moves `isrecord` out of `llm/messages.ts` without preserving that module's current export surface for `index.ts`, `db.ts`, `tool-calls.ts`, and `selectedclips.ts`, so the refactor plan can break four existing imports unless it adds a re-export or rewires those callers. (flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the actual export surface in `supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/llm/messages.ts` and its consumers. step 6 says to 'remove local `isrecord`' from `messages.ts` and import it from `utils.ts`, but without also preserving `messages.ts` as an exporter or rewiring `index.ts`, `db.ts`, `tool-calls.ts`, and `selectedclips.ts`, that change would break the module graph immediately. (flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the render-gating cleanup plan against remotion's runtime exports in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/cancel-render.js:46-70`. `cancelrender()` stores an error and throws to abort the render; it is not a benign cleanup for an abandoned `delayrender` handle, so step 2's instruction to call `cancelrender(handle)` on unmount is technically wrong and would abort preview or export with an error. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked how remotion itself acquires delay handles in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/iframe.js:8-18`. remotion's own components create the handle synchronously with `usestate(() => delayrender(...))`; the plan says 'calls delayrender() on mount', which reads like an effect-time action and leaves the initial-frame blocking behavior underspecified compared with the actual library pattern. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

A test that only checks one surface is not enough for rollout if another surface can still accept stale schema output, unsafe source, a missing asset, or a cross-project artifact.\n+\n+### Existing anchors to keep and extend\n+\n+Reigh already has several useful anchors:\n+\n+- `supabase/functions/ai-generate-sequence/index.test.ts`: edge entrypoint coverage for the trusted sequence generator.\n+- `supabase/functions/ai-generate-sequence/sequence-validation.ts`: trusted v1 server validator that should continue rejecting code, raw URLs, arbitrary animation refs, unknown root fields, and asset references outside the allowed registry set.\n+- `src/tools/video-editor/sequences/validation.test.ts`: browser-side trusted draft validator coverage.\n+- `src/tools/video-editor/sequences/materialize.ts`: materialization boundary for converting allowed asset keys into render-time URLs without mutating persisted params.\n+- `src/tools/video-editor/lib/renderRouter.test.ts`: render routing coverage, including unknown and absent clip types.\n+- `supabase/functions/timeline-import/handler.test.ts`: import coverage for `asset_registry`, versioned updates, `expected_version`, `version_mismatch`, create/update behavior, and ownership-sensitive calls.\n+\n+The shared schema package at `../../banodoco-workspace/packages/timeline-schema` already has the release-critical drift gates:\n+\n+- `package.json` scripts: `npm run build`, `npm run gen:python`, `npm run check:codegen`, and `npm test`.\n+- `Makefile`: `make check` runs `check-codegen` and tests.\n+- `scripts/check-codegen.sh`: regenerates TypeScript-derived JSON Schema and Python types, then fails when generated artifacts are stale.\n+- `typescript/tests/resolveTheme.test.ts` and `tests/test_materialize_output.py`: current TypeScript/Python contract tests.\n+- Generated outputs: `python/banodoco_timeline_schema/timeline.schema.json` and `python/banodoco_timeline_schema/generated.py`. These must be diff-checked, not manually edited.\n+\n+ArtAgents already has parity anchors that should be kept in the rollout gate:\n+\n+- `tests/test_schema_contract.py`: timeline/assets examples, schema roundtrips, and generated type drift.\n+- `tests/test_publish.py`: publish behavior around assets, tokens, `expected_version`, and `timeline-import`.\n+- `tests/test_render_remotion_registry.py`: local Remotion render wrapper and registry handling.\n+- `tests/test_open_in_reigh.py`: manual handoff behavior and guardrails.\n+- `tests/test_validate.py`: ArtAgents timeline validation behavior.\n+- `tests/test_pure_generative_pipeline.py`, `tests/test_composition_primitives.py`, and `tests/test_hype_cut_invariants.py`: pipeline and composition invariants that protect generated timeline structure.\n+\n+### Required lane test matrix\n+\n+Trusted v1 must stay strict:\n+\n+- Positive: a known good trusted draft generated by `ai-generate-sequence` validates on the server, validates in the browser, inserts through the existing sequence draft path, persists as ordinary `TimelineConfig`, and renders without artifact records.\n+- Negative: `code`, `component`, `jsx`, `tsx`, `html`, `script`, `imports`, `source`, `render`, arbitrary animation refs, raw URLs, unknown root keys, and asset keys outside the allowed set are rejected in both `sequence-validation.ts` and `src/tools/video-editor/sequences/validation.test.ts`.\n+- Regression: adding schema-sequence or module support must not change the default `SequenceCreatorPanel` behavior or allow trusted v1 drafts to carry generated source.\n+\n+Schema-sequences need compiler and import coverage:\n+\n+- Positive: a valid schema-sequence source compiles deterministically into ordinary timeline JSON plus asset registry JSON, validates against regenerated `@banodoco/timeline-schema` outputs, and imports through `timeline-import`.\n+- Negative: malformed operations, missing required fields, oversized schemas, missing assets, raw URLs where only registry keys are allowed, unsupported media or transition declarations, schema version mismatches, and stale schema outputs are rejected before persistence.\n+- Determinism: the same source, compiler version, asset registry, and schema version must produce the same compiled timeline and artifact hash.\n+- Compatibility: compiled clips use current supported clip types, preserve ordinary render routing, and do not require existing timeline rows to migrate.\n+\n+Generated Remotion modules need artifact, sandbox, and router coverage:\n+\n+- Positive: a valid proposed artifact manifest with declared props, declared assets, dependency metadata, and a project-owned `artifact_id` can route to the worker path when a clip has `clip.generation.sequence_lane === 'remotion_module'`.\n+- Negative: missing `artifact_id`, artifact project mismatch, unsupported imports, undeclared dependencies, raw network access, raw URLs outside declared assets, missing assets, malformed props, oversized bundles/manifests, code injection through manifest fields, timeouts, memory or frame-budget failures, and failed worker validation must produce structured failures.\n+- Router safety: unknown clip types and absent clip types still follow the existing client/placeholder fallback unless explicit module lane metadata is present; a module-lane clip with missing or invalid artifact metadata must fail closed rather than route to the client renderer.\n+- Browser safety: tests should assert the editor never imports or evaluates generated module source. Browser previews may only read artifact status, thumbnails, rendered previews, placeholders, or schema-derived fallback data.\n+\n+`timeline-import` remains the persistence gate:\n+\n+- Positive: Reigh, ArtAgents, and future artifact APIs publish compiled output through `{ project_id, timeline_id, timeline, asset_registry, expected_version, create_if_missing }` using user JWT auth and versioned update semantics.\n+- Negative: invalid UUIDs, cross-user access, existing timeline rows from another project, service-role publish attempts on the user path, invalid `TimelineConfig`, invalid `asset_registry` envelope, version conflicts, stale `expected_version`, and missing ownership checks fail before writes.\n+- Concurrency: `version_mismatch` responses must be asserted for stale writes, and callers must not silently overwrite newer editor changes.\n+\n+### Drift and CI gates\n+\n+Every implementation PR for this architecture should have an explicit test gate list. The minimum gate is:\n+\n+- Reigh: run the focused sequence, render router, and timeline import suites that include `supabase/functions/ai-generate-sequence/index.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/sequences/validation.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/lib/renderRouter.test.ts`, and `supabase/functions/timeline-import/handler.test.ts`.\n+- Shared schema: run `make check` or the equivalent `npm run build`, `npm run check:codegen`, `npm test`, and Python tests from `../../banodoco-workspace/packages/timeline-schema`.\n+- ArtAgents: run the schema/publish/render validation tests covering `tests/test_schema_contract.py`, `tests/test_publish.py`, `tests/test_render_remotion_registry.py`, `tests/test_open_in_reigh.py`, and `tests/test_validate.py`.\n+- Drift: fail CI if regenerated `timeline.schema.json`, `generated.py`, or ArtAgents generated Remotion types are stale after codegen.\n+- Security negatives: require explicit tests for code injection, raw URLs, missing assets, oversized schemas, unsupported imports, unknown clip types, stale schema outputs, timeouts, version conflicts, and cross-user access before enabling schema-sequence or generated-module flags beyond internal allowlists.\n+\n+### Review rules for new tests\n+\n+Tests should assert failure reasons, not only rejection booleans. The implementation needs enough structured error output to tell whether a failure came from schema validation, asset validation, artifact ownership, router selection, worker sandboxing, timeout, or optimistic-lock conflict.\n+\n+Manual editor review can supplement rollout, but it cannot replace automated gates for lane selection, schema drift, ownership, import versioning, and generated-code sandbox boundaries.\n+\n ## Non-Negotiable Constraints\n \n - The trusted v1 sequence creator remains the default path. Future schema or code lanes must be gated additions, not replacements for `SequenceCreatorPanel` and the current `ai-generate-sequence` draft flow.\n - Trusted drafts remain data-only. The v1 validator must continue rejecting generated code, raw URLs, imports, arbitrary animation refs, unknown top-level fields, and asset references outside the selected or attached registry set.\n@@\n - **SD-GENSEQ-017** — Require ArtAgents to consume regenerated shared schema outputs before publishing generated sequence artifacts. _load_bearing: true_\n   Rationale: ArtAgents already publishes timeline/assets JSON into Reigh. Schema-sequence and module parity depends on using the same generated schema/types as Reigh, not a handwritten or stale local contract.\n+\n+- **SD-GENSEQ-018** — Make validation and tests lane-specific, with generated lanes failing closed. _load_bearing: true_\n+  Rationale: Trusted drafts, schema-sequences, and generated modules have different risk boundaries. Tests must prove each boundary independently so unsafe artifacts cannot fall through to ordinary client rendering or persistence.\n+\n+- **SD-GENSEQ-019** — Treat shared-schema codegen drift as a release blocker. _load_bearing: true_\n+  Rationale: Reigh, timeline-import, worker payloads, and ArtAgents publishing depend on the same generated schema and Python/TypeScript outputs. Stale generated files recreate the cross-repo mismatch this plan is removing.\n+\n+- **SD-GENSEQ-020** — Require negative security coverage before enabling advanced lanes outside internal allowlists. _load_bearing: true_\n+  Rationale: Schema-sequence and generated-module rollout should not depend on manual inspection for code injection, raw URLs, missing assets, unsupported imports, timeouts, version conflicts, or cross-user access.\n*** End Patch\n"

        Debt watch items (do not make these worse):
- [DEBT] agent-chat-rendering: removing the duplicate assistant turn may hide message_user text if the frontend only renders assistant-role turns as chat bubbles. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] agent-chat-undo-integration: agent chat edits arrive via query invalidation/realtime polling and will bypass the undo stack because those paths are marked skiphistory. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] agent-tool-utils: agent-tool-utils: step 6 moves `isrecord` out of `llm/messages.ts` without preserving that module's current export surface for `index.ts`, `db.ts`, `tool-calls.ts`, and `selectedclips.ts`, so the refactor plan can break four existing imports unless it adds a re-export or rewires those callers. (flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the actual export surface in `supabase/functions/ai-timeline-agent/llm/messages.ts` and its consumers. step 6 says to 'remove local `isrecord`' from `messages.ts` and import it from `utils.ts`, but without also preserving `messages.ts` as an exporter or rewiring `index.ts`, `db.ts`, `tool-calls.ts`, and `selectedclips.ts`, that change would break the module graph immediately. (flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the render-gating cleanup plan against remotion's runtime exports in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/cancel-render.js:46-70`. `cancelrender()` stores an error and throws to abort the render; it is not a benign cleanup for an abandoned `delayrender` handle, so step 2's instruction to call `cancelrender(handle)` on unmount is technically wrong and would abort preview or export with an error. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked how remotion itself acquires delay handles in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/iframe.js:8-18`. remotion's own components create the handle synchronously with `usestate(() => delayrender(...))`; the plan says 'calls delayrender() on mount', which reads like an effect-time action and leaves the initial-frame blocking behavior underspecified compared with the actual library pattern. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the new `useaudioparam()` sketch against `src/tools/video-editor/effects/compileeffect.tsx:1-2`. the plan defines it in terms of `interpolate(audio[binding.source], ...)` but does not explicitly import `interpolate` into the new hook file or simplify it to straight arithmetic, so the helper's implementation contract is still looser than it needs to be. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked revised step 2.4 against `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useclipresize.ts:76-100`. the plan still says to clamp audio by writing back to `action.end`, but the current hook treats the callback `action` as input data and then creates fresh row actions from it. mutating that caller-owned object is unnecessary and risks coupling the resize hook to outside references instead of using a local `clampedend` variable. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the no-duration-fetch decision against `src/tools/travel-between-images/hooks/video/useshotfinalvideos.ts:19-37`, `src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.ts:17-35`, and `src/tools/video-editor/compositions/visualclip.tsx:114-123`. the repository still derives clip length from `to - from`, and the final-video query still provides no duration metadata, so the revised plan still cannot prove that `to: endtime - starttime` is safe for shorter source media; a short final video can still be asked to play longer than its actual content. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the hand-built replacement clip against the existing insert path in `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useassetmanagement.ts:201-252,262-271` and serialization in `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/usetimelinecommit.ts:210-216`. the revised `timelineeditor` sketch still bypasses current insertion invariants such as manual-track geometry defaults and explicit `cliporder` updates, so replacement clips on manual visual tracks will not be initialized the same way as other inserted video clips and may serialize in a different per-track order. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the new `pinnedshotgroupsoverride` design is still underspecified against `materializedata()`. `assembletimelinedata()` computes `stablesignature` from the config it receives, so if the executor literally follows step 2.4 and overwrites `pinnedshotgroups` on an already-materialized `timelinedata` before `commitdata()`, the saved config and the cached `stablesignature` will diverge unless the data is rebuilt from the updated config. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the revised grouped-drag plan fixes the pointer-down selection regression, but it still leaves `pinnedshotgroup.trackid` stale on cross-track moves. the data model stores `trackid`, and current drag/move helpers only update rows/meta/clip order, so a pinned group dragged to another track would keep pointing at the old track unless the drag commit also patches group metadata. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked step 2.4 against `materializedata()` in `usetimelinecommit` and `assembletimelinedata()` in `timeline-data.ts`. the plan still says to overwrite `pinnedshotgroups` after `materializedata()` returns, but `assembletimelinedata()` computes `stablesignature` from the config it receives, so mutating the config afterward would leave signature-derived state stale unless the data is rebuilt from the updated config.
